title: AI in Disguise—Quasi-Experimental Analysis of a Large-Scale Deployment of AI-Generated Ads
authors: Yannick Exner; Jochen Hartmann; Ziqian Ding; Shunyuan Zhang; Oded Netzer
managerial_implications: AI-generated ads have heterogeneous performance depending partly on whether they appear AI-generated. The quasi-experimental comparison does not detect an average click-rate disadvantage, which does not prove equivalence. Evaluate accuracy, provenance, and downstream outcomes alongside clicks.
agency_assessment: Realistic synthetic imagery can obscure provenance or misrepresent experience. Verify substantive claims and disclose origin where consequential.
evidence_basis: Full abstract in Crossref or OpenAlex metadata; preliminary interpretation

title: The Effects of Search Interface on Consumer Preferences: Evidence from a Randomized Experiment
authors: Jia Liu; Olivier Toubia
managerial_implications: Search filters change exploration and measured preferences, not merely transaction speed. A randomized interface experiment finds changes in prices paid, attribute weights, and market concentration. Evaluate navigation and preference formation alongside conversion.
agency_assessment: Interface restrictions can shape which attributes people learn to value. Preserve useful filtering and opportunities to reconsider.
evidence_basis: Full abstract in Crossref or OpenAlex metadata; preliminary interpretation

authors: Seung Hyun Kim; On Amir; Kenneth C. Wilbur
managerial_implications: Tip-request language changes tipping in field experiments, with effects varying across app and web channels. Managers should evaluate worker compensation, customer spending, and later demand. A demand response does not reveal whether customers felt pressured.
agency_assessment: Norm messages can turn a voluntary payment into perceived obligation. Keep declining easy and distinguish tips from required charges.
